title: (No AI) Midjourney bought the astrology app Co-Star
author: Emma Roth
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/STK414_AI_CHATBOT_E-1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Midjourney, which has gone from generating AI cat images to [full-body ultrasound scans](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/952011/midjourney-medical-ai-ultrasound-scan), is getting into a new field: astrology. The AI startup [announced on Thursday](https://updates.midjourney.com/midjourneys-first-acquisition/) that it has acquired the personalized astrology app Co-Star, as reported [earlier by _Bloomberg_](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-24/ai-startup-midjourney-buys-astrology-app-co-star-and-is-building-its-own-apps).

Co-Star is a free app that offers daily horoscopes and allows you to check your compatibility with friends. As noted on the [app's FAQ page](https://www.costarastrology.com/faq), it combines human insight, data from NASA, and AI to deliver personalized advice for users each day. The terms of Midjourney's deal, which reportedly closed in spring, haven't been disclosed.

title: (No AI) You can’t ignore Google Zero anymore
author: David Pierce
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/VRG_VST_20260724_Site.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

The web and Google [once had a deal](https://www.theverge.com/24067997/robots-txt-ai-text-file-web-crawlers-spiders): Google collects data and indexes webpages and in exchange sends oceans of traffic to websites. The deal wasn't perfect and certainly made Google more money than it made the websites, but it worked for a long time. Now, however, [the deal seems to be dead](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/20/technology/google-ai-open-web.html?unlocked_article_code=1.zVA.L7zf._L5VDoBJCS4f&smid=url-share). And the web is being forced to reckon with what happens when the Google traffic dries up.

On [this episode of _The Vergecast_](https://pod.link/vergecast), David and Nilay talk about the week's Google Zero news, including Reddit's interest in [getting out of an AI training deal](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/969104/reddit-might-cut-ties-with-google-as-traffic-drops), and the publishers considering blocking Google from crawling their sites altogether.
